  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is this Node users API checkout; intake is read-only and makes no changes or server starts. S2 [outcome]: API callers need create and carefully confirmed delete operations; discovery or the recorded defaults in Q1, Q3 and Q4 settle actors and contracts. S3 [outcome and fact]: Expose pagination while preserving existing returns and verify the short final page; the inspected paginator uses floor division and omits a partial final page, while no usual page size was found; Q2 and Q5 govern the unresolved interface and size. S4 [boundary]: Keep Node built-ins and a simple implementation with no dependencies. S5 [outcome and assumption]: Retain an in-memory runtime store and durable restart recovery; Q6 and Q8 address storage, concurrency, lifetime and visibility. S6 [boundary]: Later work must run improve until it finds only trivial changes, fan handler and test work out in parallel, and perform code review; Q11 and Q15 establish available workflow instructions and verification. S7 [outcome and discovery lead]: Preserve IDs for next-quarter Kestrel migration; search authorized project or team workspaces, migration documentation, relevant channels, private repositories and owners as leads, not verified sources; Q7 blocks an ID compatibility claim until evidence is found, and sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. S10 [boundary]: Preserve existing endpoint responses, including individual-user success and not-found responses; Q2 resolves the pagination interaction. Delivery [authority and visibility]: The named checkout is the authorized target; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and any deployed outcome exists only after release; no deployment target is named.
